title: Frontend Is Only Visual UI & Styling
description: Belief that frontend development is limited to colors and layout rather than state management, performance, network requests, and security.
indicators: Believing all complex logic must execute on the backend
Ignoring client-side state architectures
correction: Frontend engineering encompasses rich client state, routing, caching, accessibility, network synchronization, and high-performance DOM updates in the browser.

title: JavaScript Replaces HTML and CSS
description: Belief that writing everything in JavaScript eliminates the need to understand HTML semantics and CSS cascade mechanics.
indicators: Using <div> for every interactive control
Re-implementing basic browser navigation in custom script
correction: JavaScript manipulates the DOM; HTML provides semantic meaning and accessibility, and CSS provides hardware-accelerated rendering.

title: HTML, CSS, and JS are Interchangeable
description: Belief that HTML, CSS, and JavaScript do the same things and any one of them can replace the other two completely.
indicators: Trying to write calculation logic in HTML
Using JS animations when pure CSS transitions suffice
correction: Each technology in the triad has a distinct, specialized role: HTML is structure/meaning, CSS is presentation/layout, and JS is runtime behavior.

title: Frontend Directly Connects to Databases
description: Belief that browser JavaScript can or should directly connect to production database servers (like PostgreSQL or MongoDB) with credentials.
indicators: Looking for DB connection strings in client JS
Believing the browser directly holds SQL database tables
correction: Frontend code runs on untrusted client machines and communicates with backend servers over HTTP/WebSockets; the server securely handles database queries.

title: Websites Are Purely Static Documents
description: Belief that web pages only load once as inert text documents and cannot execute dynamic applications in the browser.
indicators: Thinking all updates require a full page refresh from the server
correction: Modern web applications run rich client-side code that dynamically updates the DOM, handles events, and synchronizes data asynchronously.

title: All HTML Tags Must Have Closing Tags
description:
Belief that void elements like , , and
require separate or closing tags.
indicators:
Writing or

in standard HTML5
correction: Void elements are self-contained and forbidden from having closing tags or inner content in standard HTML5. In standard HTML5, void elements never have closing tags.

title: Attributes Belong in Closing Tags
description: Belief that attributes like class, id, or src can or should be repeated inside the closing tag </tag>.
indicators: Writing </a href='url'> or </div class='box'>
correction: Attributes configure an element and must ONLY appear in the opening tag. Closing tags only contain the element name preceded by a slash (e.g. ).

title: Element and Tag Are Identical Terms
description: Confusing the opening/closing tags with the entire DOM element node that encompasses tags, attributes, and inner content.
indicators:
Referring to an entire paragraph node as just 'the

tag'
correction:
A tag is the markup syntax used to denote boundaries (

and

), while an element is the complete component including opening tag, attributes, content, and closing tag.

title: Attribute Quotes Are Interchangeable with Spaces
description: Belief that multi-word attribute values do not require quotes (e.g. class=btn primary instead of class='btn primary').
indicators: Writing class=btn primary
Omitting quotes on URLs containing parameters
correction: Without quotes, spaces delimit separate attributes, turning 'primary' into an unintended boolean attribute rather than part of the class value.

title: HTML Tags Can Overlap Arbitrarily
description:
Belief that elements can open and close out of hierarchical order, such as

Hello

.
indicators: Opening child before parent and closing parent before child
correction: HTML elements form a strict hierarchical tree: the most recently opened element must be closed before its parent element can close.

title: Padding and Margin Are the Same
description: Confusing internal content clearance (padding) with external spacing between elements (margin).
indicators: Applying margin when expecting background color expansion
Using padding to push sibling elements away
correction: Padding sits inside the border and is covered by backgrounds; margin sits outside the border and creates space between sibling boxes.

title: justify-content Always Aligns Horizontally
description: Assuming justify-content is always horizontal, regardless of flex-direction.
indicators: Expecting align-items to align horizontally in column layout
correction: justify-content aligns along the MAIN axis (horizontal in row, vertical in column); align-items aligns along the CROSS axis.

title: justify-content Moves Individual Child Items
description: Belief that justify-content is a property applied to individual child items rather than the parent flex container to distribute all children.
indicators: Applying justify-content: space-between on a child <div> instead of the parent container
correction: justify-content is a container-level property that coordinates the collective distribution of all child items along the main axis.

title: align-items Always Centers Horizontally
description: Assuming align-items controls horizontal centering regardless of flex-direction.
indicators: Setting flex-direction: column and expecting align-items: center to center vertically
correction: align-items always operates on the cross axis. When flex-direction is column, the cross axis is horizontal, so align-items centers horizontally.

title: display: flex Affects All Nested Descendants
description: Belief that setting display: flex on a top-level container turns grandchildren and deep descendants into flex items.
indicators: Expecting grandchild elements to automatically align into a row without setting display: flex on their parent
correction: display: flex only creates a flex context for immediate direct children. Nested elements require their own display: flex declarations.

title: Flexbox Requires Hardcoded Margins for Spacing
description: Using margin-right: 20px on every flex item instead of leveraging justify-content or the gap property.
indicators: Adding hardcoded pixel margins on flex children and breaking last-child alignment
correction: Flexbox containers natively space items using justify-content (e.g. space-between) and the modern CSS gap property.

title: console.log() Returns a Value from a Function
description: Confusing printing output to the developer console with returning a value to the calling expression.
indicators: Writing const result = add(1, 2) where add only does console.log
Expecting console.log to provide data to callers
correction: console.log writes text to the DevTools console and evaluates to undefined. return explicitly passes a value back to whoever called the function.

title: console.log() Outputs Data to Calling Code
description: Believing that console.log(x) sends x back to the variable receiving the function call.
indicators: Expecting let x = calculate(5) to receive data when calculate only has console.log
correction: console.log is purely a debugging side effect for humans; only return sends data to the executing JavaScript program.

title: Functions Auto-Return the Last Defined Variable
description: Believing JavaScript works like some languages where the last evaluated expression is automatically returned without a return keyword.
indicators: Defining let sum = a + b inside a function and omitting return sum
correction: In JavaScript standard functions, if there is no explicit return statement, the function execution finishes and evaluates to undefined.

title: Code After return Continues to Run
description: Believing statements written below a return statement inside a function block will still execute.
indicators: Writing cleanup or logging code directly below return x
correction: The return statement immediately halts function execution and exits the function frame; subsequent code is unreachable.

title: Debugging by Random Guesswork
description: Randomly modifying syntax without forming a hypothesis about why the failure occurs.
indicators: Adding random ! or ; or changing random CSS values without inspecting DevTools
correction: Systematic debugging involves observing symptoms, inspecting DevTools console and DOM state, forming a hypothesis, and testing targeted fixes.

title: Click Failure Is Always a JS Calculation Bug
description: Assuming that when a button click does nothing, the bug is inside the calculation function rather than a broken querySelector or missing event listener.
indicators: Rewriting math logic when the button handler was never attached to the DOM node
correction: Trace the entire event chain: check HTML ID matching, querySelector resolution, event listener binding, and finally the callback logic.

title: CSS Typos Throw Visible Console Errors
description: Believing misspelled CSS property names (like displau: flex or colr: red) will trigger error logs in the JavaScript console.
indicators: Checking only the JS console when CSS layout fails to apply
correction: Browsers follow CSS fault tolerance rules and silently ignore unrecognized properties without throwing runtime exceptions.

title: Cannot read properties of null Means Corrupt JS
description: Thinking 'Cannot read properties of null (reading addEventListener)' means the browser's JavaScript engine is broken.
indicators: Believing addEventListener is missing from the browser API
correction: This error means document.querySelector returned null because the element selector ID/class did not match any element in the HTML DOM.

title: const Freezes Nested Object/Array Values
description: Believing const makes internal properties or elements immutable, rather than preventing reassignment of the variable binding itself.
indicators: Believing array.push() will fail on a const array
Assuming const deep-freezes objects
correction: const locks the binding/reference itself. It prevents pointing the identifier to a new value, but does not deeply freeze the internal contents of mutable objects.

title: let and const Can Be Read Before Initialization
description: Believing let and const behave like legacy var declarations and return undefined when accessed before their declaration line.
indicators: Accessing variables before let/const declaration
Ignoring the Temporal Dead Zone
correction: Accessing let or const variables before their line of declaration triggers a ReferenceError due to the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ).

title: String and Number Addition Performs Math
description: Expecting '5' + 3 to evaluate to the number 8 rather than the concatenated string '53'.
indicators: Expecting string addition to cast strings to numbers automatically
Surprised by '53' output
correction: In JavaScript, if either operand of the + operator is a string, it performs string concatenation rather than mathematical addition.

title: Single Equals Compares Values
description: Using = instead of === to compare two values in expressions or if statements.
indicators: Writing if (x = 5)
Confusing assignment with equality comparison
correction: Single equals (=) is the assignment operator. Strict equality comparison requires triple equals (===).

title: Loose Equality (==) Is Safe for General Use
description: Believing double equals is interchangeable with triple equals without consequences.
indicators: Using == by default
Unaware of coercion edge cases like '' == 0 being true
correction: Loose equality applies complex type coercion rules leading to surprising true results (e.g. 0 == '' is true). Strict equality (===) prevents these bugs.

title: Assignment Inside if Evaluates Previous Value
description: Believing if (role = 'admin') checks the current role instead of assigning 'admin' and always evaluating to truthy.
indicators: if branch always executing regardless of input
Overwriting variable values inside conditionals
correction: Assignment expressions evaluate to the assigned value. Assigning a non-empty string in an if statement always evaluates to true.

title: Independent if Statements Are Mutually Exclusive
description: Expecting sequential if statements to stop checking after the first matching branch without using else if.
indicators: Writing multiple if blocks for grading brackets and getting multiple outputs
correction: Each independent if statement is evaluated independently. Use else if to create mutually exclusive branches where only the first true branch executes.

title: switch Cases Automatically Break
description: Assuming matching a case in a switch statement automatically stops execution without a break statement.
indicators: Omitting break statements and observing downstream case execution
correction: Without a break statement, execution falls through into subsequent case blocks even if their criteria do not match.

title: All Strings Are Truthy
description: Believing an empty string '' evaluates to true in boolean conditionals.
indicators: Assuming if ('') runs the truthy branch
correction: An empty string '' is falsy in JavaScript, alongside 0, null, undefined, NaN, and false.

title: Loop Condition Defines When to Stop
description: Believing the condition in for or while loops specifies the exit condition rather than the continuation condition.
indicators: Writing while (count === 10) expecting it to loop until 10
correction: Loop conditions specify when the loop should CONTINUE running, not when it should terminate. The loop stops when the condition evaluates to false.

title: Using <= on Length with Zero-Indexed Collections
description: Using i <= length in a loop counter, attempting to access an out-of-bounds element at index equal to length.
indicators: Iterating i <= items.length and encountering undefined on final iteration
correction: Zero-indexed sequences of length N have valid indices 0 through N-1. Use i < length to stay strictly within valid bounds.

title: while Loops Advance State Automatically
description: Believing while loops automatically increment loop variables without explicit statements in the loop body.
indicators: Writing while (count < 5) { console.log(count); } without count++
correction: while loops do not advance state automatically. The loop body must explicitly update variables involved in the condition to ensure termination.

title: Array Indexing Begins at 1
description: Believing array elements start at index 1, leading to missing the first element (index 0) or reading undefined past the end.
indicators: Accessing array[1] to retrieve the first element
Using index <= array.length
correction: JavaScript arrays are 0-indexed: the first element is at [0] and the final element is at [array.length - 1].

title: map() Mutates the Input Array in Place
description: Believing map() changes the existing array directly rather than returning a newly allocated array containing the transformed values.
indicators: Calling array.map() without capturing the return value
Expecting the source array elements to change in place
correction: map() does not alter the original array. It allocates and returns a new array with the mapped results.

title: filter() Transforms or Converts Element Values
description: Believing filter() can alter element values (like map) rather than solely deciding whether each element is included based on a boolean return value.
indicators: Returning modified items inside filter callback instead of boolean true/false
correction: filter() only checks if each element should be included (truthy) or excluded (falsy); it does not transform the elements themselves.

title: Dot Notation Evaluates Variable Names Dynamically
description: Believing user.field looks up the property named by the variable field rather than the literal property named field.
indicators: Writing user.fieldName when fieldName is a dynamic argument
Expecting dot notation to evaluate expressions
correction: Dot notation (user.field) looks up the exact identifier field. To evaluate a variable or expression as a property key, bracket notation (user[field]) must be used.

title: Reading Nonexistent Properties Throws an Error
description: Believing that accessing a property not present on an existing object throws a runtime exception rather than evaluating to undefined.
indicators: Assuming obj.missingKey will crash the script
Failing to check for undefined
correction: Accessing an undefined property on a valid object returns undefined without throwing. A TypeError only occurs if accessing a property on undefined or null.

title: Writing Monolithic Scripts Instead of Composed Functions
description: Believing writing an entire application as one huge linear script is faster and simpler than breaking it down into small, tested, single-purpose functions.
indicators: Putting all state updates, math, filtering, and printing inside a single block
Duplicating counting logic across multiple places
correction: Breaking programs into small functions with clear input contracts makes each piece independently testable, reusable, and easy to maintain.
